author: National Geographic
description:
Presented by @ROLEX . Rehabilitating baby pangolins doesn't just mean keeping them safe and fed, it also involves teaching them how to keep themselves fed in the wild. That's why pangolin handlers at the Tikki Hywood Foundation take young pangolins for walks in the woods every day, showing them where to find the thousands of ants and termites they need to forage daily.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Learn more about the intensive work that goes into pangolin rehabilitation in the October edition of National Geographic: https://on.natgeo.com/0b2048

Video by Marcus Westberg
title: Teaching a young pangolin how to feed itself #Rolex #PerpetualPlanet #AfricaEarthsWildHome

author: National Geographic
description:
Following his dramatic conquest of the ancient world, Alexander the Great was crowned pharaoh of Egypt and established the legendary coastal city of Alexandria. In this full episode of Lost Treasures of Egypt from National Geographic, join archaeologists as they venture deep into catacombs and sacred ruins in search of the legendary ruler's lost tomb. 

While searching for the tomb’s location, one of the greatest and most enduring mysteries in archaeology, teams uncover new insights into Alexander's reign in ancient Egypt. Was Alexander the greatest general in history? How did he conquer Egypt? Explore how the Macedonian king became pharaoh.
